newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos orders arrest of MP in sex case.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos orders arrest of MP in sex case.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Monday personally ordered the arrest of a legislator who has evaded arrest for nearly two weeks after being charged with the statutory rape of an 11-year-old girl.

"The authorities concerned (had) better capture, arrest and jail him," Ramos told reporters, adding he was dismayed at the police failure to locate congressman Romeo Jalosjos, a member of the president's ruling coalition.
Jalosjos has avoided arrest since a Manila judge on December 26 issued 14 separate warrants of arrest against him for two counts of statutory rape and 12 acts of lasciviousness.
Newspapers have said police failure to bring him to justice could further erode public confidence in the judicial system.

"Jalosjos' ability to evade 14 arrest warrants underlines (poll) findings on the ability of the rich and powerful to circumvent the judicial process," the Philippine Daily Inquirer newspaper said in a recent editorial.
"It also illustrates the paralysis of sheriffs and police when they are ordered to serve judicial warrants on powerful officials."

State prosecutors said Jalosjos had sex with the girl several times in his Manila apartment last year, paying her amounts ranging up to 10,000 pesos ($385) each time. They said the girl's father brought her to the politician in exchange for money.
The father faces a separate charge of exploitation.

Some Manila newspapers said earlier this month that Jalosjos had left the country for the Malaysian state of Sabah, but officials of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) said on Monday they believed he was still in the Philippines, most likely around Manila.
